paragraphs.text: "The cathars have taught me many things, but I will never forget the hard, honest work that first callused my hands."
For some customers, the old apothecary shop still opens its doors.
She now sees only Emrakul's visions.
Upon discovering what had become of her sisters, Sigarda could only weep.
"Honorable tactics are for honorable foes. These werewolves are preying on innocent travelers. I'll stab them in the back while they sleep if I have to."
Some cathars succumbed to despair at Avacyn's unmaking. The rest redoubled their efforts to carry out her work.
Avacyn's holy warriors kept hope alive in her darkest hours. Now they will carry that hope across Innistrad.
"I will join you so that you will not yet join me."
In the town's final stand, they overcame the snarling beasts as well as months of insidious distrust.
She now hears only Emrakul's murmurs.
Immune to the physical warping caused by Emrakul, geists proved to be some of humanity's most important allies.
"Our enemies will soon discover that we are not as meek as they had believed."
In life, they were a motley crew: farmers, lords, cutpurses, priests. In death, they are united in singular, benevolent purpose.
The landlord drove off the elderly couple to repossess their home. Eventually, the couple possessed it back.
"A boon from the angels should never be cast aside." —Manfried Ulmach, Chief Inquisitor
"Even in our darkest times, Avacyn's light still guides us."
"Ghoulcallers trying to get in, geists trying to get out . . . . This duty is never dull."
"In these halls there is no pass or fail. Your true test comes with the first full moon."
Avacyn's most devout would forgo the Blessed Sleep to keep vigil.
"If you must go out at night, bring a mob." —Master of the Elgaud Cathars
It conducts the souls of the righteous to their blessed rest and the spirits of the evil to justice.
"We fight not for Avacyn, but for her ideals; not for the church, but for its people." —Thalia, Guardian of Thraben
"If you've been at this as long as I have, nothing can surprise you. That's the hope, at least."
Odric took no joy in violence but neither did he mourn for the twisted things he dispatched. All that mattered were the lives he had saved.
Vampires from every bloodline mingled together, all swelling with pride to be seen at the event of the century.
Not content to nudge vases and chill drawing rooms, some geists muster spectral armies to claw at the hearts of the living.
Serpents leave their eggs in the cold and inky depths...
...knowing their hatchlings are more fearsome than anything else that might come along.
"Don't worry everyone—I hear hoofbeats! The Gavony Riders are coming to save us!" —Adin, Moorland villager
"So much for neighborly hospitality!"
"Unfortunately, all my test animals have died or escaped, so I shall be the final subject. I feel no fear. This is a momentous night." —Laboratory notes, final entry
"Garl, adjust the slurry dispensers. Garl, fetch more corpses. Garl, quit crying and give me your brain tissue. If he doesn't stop being so rude, I'm quitting."
The time had come for him to share his findings.
Seagrafs yield an abundance of resources for stitchers and ghoulcallers alike.
Tamil had always wanted a closer look at a geist's lantern. Now he had an eternity to study one.
"There's no question that these waters are treacherous, but if there's one thing I've learned in all my years of sailing . . ."
". . . it's that the lure of the sea is impossible to ignore."
Only one vault was great enough to hold Emrakul.
Val didn't know what the silent geist was offering . . .
. . . but she knew it would be rude to refuse.
"It always amazes me what perfectly good things people throw away." —Ludevic, necro-alchemist
"Geralf's prowess continues to grow. He can now replicate my own creations with near-perfect accuracy." —Ludevic's laboratory notes
Progress comes at a price.
"Let those idiot priests tremble! A new era in unlife begins here and now. Oglor, raise the lightning vane!" —Stitcher Geralf
"Fool! Can't you see the tide has turned against you?"
Time is a marvelous plaything.
"It serves as evidence of the ancient power of the deep, a reminder that the sea is the only thing worthy of reverence." —Runo Stromkirk
"Either I know just the spell I need, or I'm about to."
Jenrik's tower is served by those who once sought to enter it uninvited.
"Oh no. Oh no. Oh no. Oh no, again!" —Beltstad, cathar recruit, last words
"The ravings of the mad are laced with eldritch knowledge."
"Vanya Falkenrath's paintings are astonishing. How does she manage to achieve such rich crimson hues?" —Stefan, art critic
What could be more irresistible than death?
A tragic moment pushed him to a blasphemous act.
Once he'd tasted that dark power, there was no turning back.
"If you hear a groaning noise in the cellar, don't investigate. Don't split up. Just lock the door and barricade it." —Emili, guard captain
"Great Ormendahl, I kneel before you, a fragment of your will, a servant of your tyranny. I beg you, release the strength within me!"
Bones cracked, flesh split apart, and the screams of euphoric agony gave way to unholy laughter.
"Here you go. Can't have you sleeping through your own wedding day."
"There was a time when our cages rang with wailing. Now only a handful of these whimpering fools remain."
"Soft dirt makes for light work."
"Innistrad's ghoulcallers are talented enough, but let me show you what someone with real power can create." —Liliana Vess
"Avacyn emerged from the broken Helvault, but her freedom came at a price—him." —Thalia, Knight-Cathar
"They won't be winning any beauty pageants, but they'll do the trick." —Enslow, ghoulcaller of Nephalia
"If you're not surrounded by decadence, my question to you is—why not?"
The eerie magic animating Innistrad's zombies rendered them immune to phyresis, making them crucial to the plane's defense.
On Innistrad, one person's windfall usually starts with another person lying face down in the mud.
Cover your ears and you may never hear her coming—both a blessing and a curse.
"Thank you. This blade becomes so hot in my hand, but your blood has quenched it."
Displays of Voldaren bloodlust are not restricted to glamorous banquets and lavish parties.
His mind was lost long before his flesh.
A barricade only buys time. So the wealthy buy more barricades.
"Thraben's pleas fall on deaf ears. Ours do not."
Linger on death's door and risk being invited in.
There will be no absolution.
"You were so eager to take and consume. Yet when asked to give, you refuse?"
"Humans throw rice and release doves at their weddings? How quaint."
The Falkenrath progenitor was a vicious falconer, and the line is quick to remind others of its heritage.
"Some claim that rage is a cloud that obscures thought and vision. But I can assure you—I've never seen with greater clarity."
Mist is the geists' sorrow. Wind is their pain. Fire is their vengeance.
It strikes with the fury of a tempest.
As without, so within.
"Avacyn has abandoned us! We have nothing left except what we can take!"
So many candles. So many flammables. So little time.
"Let the flames ignore the sinless."
"Writhe all you want, filth. It will do you no good."
"We're ready for anything!"
He scans for wolves, knowing there's one he can never anticipate.
Technically he never left his post. He looks after the wolf wherever it goes.
A carriage crafted from the finest materials. Horses bred from the finest stock. Skulls taken from the finest foes.
Even vampires know to travel faster when they hear howling in the Geier Reach passes.
"Hold tight. I've got a surprise for them."
Spirits disturbed by ghoulcallers become geists driven by restless anger.
"We spend our entire existence pursuing the joy of our first night's feast." —Anje Falkenrath
In a wave of spells called the Cursemute, Avacyn cleansed the world with divine fire.
The wolf's captor hid his fear, but he knew someday the runes would fail, the collar would break, and the wolf would remember his face.
"I am not its master. We are of the same pack." —Ulrich, Krallenhorde alpha
"It's right to fear those that you keep locked away." —Rahilda, Vildin-Pack alpha
It's not any fun until someone loses an eye.
"Gotcha."
"I have yet to find my equal."
"A slayer gets by on wits and reflexes." —Higa, slayer-captain of Gatstaf
"Living creatures seldom impress me. But I like this one." —Uta Falkenrath
As werewolf attacks increased, brutal weapons not seen since the Travails were dusted off and put to work.
The chant was incomprehensible, but its power was unmistakable.
"Our coven finds strength in nature and purpose in serving our communities."
"Careful now. Don't want to get the seeds stuck to your feelers like last time."
"Bury your dead deep. The boars are hungriest while the corpse is still warm." —Paulin, trapper of Somberwald
It uproots entire fengrafs to add to its twisted frame.
Emrakul does not grant wishes. Desires simply align to her will.
"While the church thinks in terms of legacies, others think in terms of eternities."
"I would fear this fight, bloodsucker, were I alone."
"The woods are not unknowable. Certainty and order are woven with the roots."
"There's a forester lives up in the highlands. Tried to sell her one of my finest axes at a bargain, but she wasn't interested." —Old Rutstein
"She even had the audacity to criticize my wares as inferior." —Old Rutstein
The renewed howling of werewolves announced the end of the Cursemute—and the beginning of Avacyn's madness.
"How do I know where aid is needed? Look around you."
He can deny his true nature for only so long.
Between stitchers, cultists, and scavengers, corpses are in high demand.
Courage alone won't keep you alive.
"More rope may not be necessary." —Kep, Lunarch inquisitor
"Remember to come back in a few years when that fungus has died off. Then we'll see what's in the chest." —Old Rutstein
Visiting a shrine at the start of a journey makes the traveler more likely to finish it.
With the cycles of day and night unspooled, the twisted sway of the moon only grew. And grew.
You can spot a werewolf-infested town by its lack of butcher shops.
Estwald's citizens don't dislike outsiders—they taste just fine.
"My angel is the flint, and I am her steel."
A soulless husk of endless hunger.
"These fiends are slightly less tolerable than you." "A sentiment that warms my heart, sister."
The hunters spent the evening celebrating their kill and the rest of the night running from it.
"We can go into the dark hand-in-hand or alone. I know which I prefer."
"I can't abide shoddy work. Whose are these?" —Ghoulcaller Gisa
"I'll lead."
"Sturdy nails make for sound sleep." —Cosper Lowe of the Silbern Guard
Meat is meat.
For the necro-alchemist, any puzzle can be solved with intelligence and harvested body parts.

"I felt compelled to take the twisted stone, and I abandoned my horse's burden to accommodate its weight. Now, its continued glow illuminates my home and warms my mind." —Garner Kroft, Moorland farmer
It comes off as easily as your own skin.
Many names and many memories bound together in grim purpose.
The rigs were outlawed except in Nephalia, where malign spirits are as plentiful as crazed inventors.
The harvest is never finished.
"There is a rich history in a blade like this." —Old Rutstein
"Its previous owners had some stories to share, I'm certain." —Old Rutstein
Entry 434: There's more to Avacyn's madness . . .
The rider set off into the eerie mist, swaddled in armor and laden with amulets.
Deadly mushrooms litter these woods, each waiting for an errant footstep to release its noxious spores.
Drownyard floods and unnatural frost made the once peaceful boardwalk deceptively treacherous.
Soothing whispers invite travelers to step closer, closer, closer . . . until they vanish soundlessly beneath the surface.
"Our world is vast, but Thraben is its heart. The cathedral must stand even if the hinterlands are lost." —Thalia, Knight-Cathar
Swirling eddies of ash hide crumbling cliffs, treacherous drops, and the slavering maws of unknown evils.
A few weed-choked gourd patches are all that remain of the proud, thriving farms that once blanketed the province.
Cries of panic echo along Kessig's narrow ravines as howlpacks herd their prey.
The Quietus Cult holds their grim ceremonies in the dark places where unburied dead litter the ground.
The bones of doomed ships jut out from the muck while the bones of their sailors molder below.
Frequent, violent storms shape the Nephalia coastline, sculpting cliffs and caves where monsters often lurk.
Riders chase the fading light recklessly through the mountains, desperate for one last glimpse of day.
With Griselbrand gone, the Skirsdag eagerly awaited another demon to claim their devotion. Ormendahl did not make them wait long.
"When belief is shaken, seek faith in yourself. That temple must never fall." —*The Teachings of Saint Traft*
The cause of each death was clear, but the pattern eluded her.
Searing light. Concussing thunder. Smoldering ash.
"As long as I learn from it, it's still science!"
"What nature creates cannot be unnatural!" —"Doctor" Zilky Grebbs
You have all the time in the world.
Old battlefields have no shortage of bodies, but the bodies are rarely intact.
"Better to be dead in a Gavony ditch than missing in the Stensia mountains." —Folk saying
"Win, lose, or die, 'tis still all the same. Devils just bedevil for the love of the game." —Gavony children's rhyme
The cryptoliths promised a tantalizing boon for opportunists—control without the requirement of mastery.
Good archers kill in one shot. Great archers confirm with two.
The gate could send hedgewitches across the world, or entice a traveler from boundaries just beyond.
An enigma as vexing as life itself.
"We must save you from yourselves."
Moorlanders speak in awe of the priests' talent for arriving just in time to drive off the wicked things that prowl the ravished parish.
"We are Odric's sword. We strike without fear, for his mind has divined how our foe will be slain."
"The harder they try to extinguish my faith, the brighter it burns in the darkness."
You don't want to see his trophy room.
The restless geists of common folk often continue their lifelong labors.
The remnants of Innistrad's corrupted angelic hosts collapsed to form the Flight of Nightmares.
"Salvation will not be granted by the Lunarch Council. It must be earned—at the edge of a sword, if necessary."
A spirit is both fettered and free—bound in some ways to its previous existence, yet able to transcend much of the corporeal.
His mind whirled with grand plans, never thinking of what might happen if he were to succeed.
"When you see a raven, head for the hills. It knows when the ghost-tide is headed in." —Sved, fisherman of Nephalia
"Dear brother, it's sweet that you have chosen to share your toys with Ludevic, but I too have found some new playmates." —Ghoulcaller Gisa
The same magic that lets geists pass through our realm can force them out of it.
"Let's start fresh, shall we?"
Without a mind, it doesn't fear death. Without a soul, it doesn't mind killing.
Subservience to greater power is the only law in the pit.
It was a family reunion to die for.
Ancient evils dwell within the burning chasm called the Ashmouth, ever ready to devour those foolish enough to travel alone.
"Try again in the next life, darling."
"Impressive." —Chandra Nalaar
"One vampire for every family member I've lost."
Gavony was their stage, and the moon their spotlight.
"Madness can't touch a mind ignited by genius."
"If you're not refining your tastes, what's the point of living forever?"
Animated by geists fused in its oak, it hungers for more life to add to its core.
"The cornfields promise a good yield this season." —Radwick, farmer of Gatstaf
"You can face any danger when all of nature is on your side."
Otto the Hunter was filled with many grand ambitions. The snake was filled only with Otto.
The Ulvenwald makes no allowances for youth. Today's newborn is either tomorrow's hunter or tomorrow's lunch.
The surviving militia members reunited with their fallen comrades sooner than they'd hoped.
Better potent than predictable.
Great devotion yields great reward.
"Faith can quicken the stones themselves with life." —Writings of Mikaeus
"Tomorrow wears yesterday's face." —Kordel the Cryptic
"Ludevic saw it in a dream and set to work immediately, every detail already known. Can such genius be taught?" —Stitcher Geralf
"Wings that once bore hope are now stained with blood. She is our guardian no longer." —Grete, cathar apostate
"You'll never believe what I heard."
Rumors are sparks: gather enough of them and something's going to catch fire.
She faced down a howlpack alone, saving her town at the cost of her life.
Since her passing, many more travelers have made it home alive.
"Metamorphosis is a process." —Laboratory notes
The final pages of the experiment log were blank. Investigators found it abandoned on a desk in the researcher's lab, open, the pages flipping in the wind from a shattered window.
Rather than consort with demons, the Quietus Cult seeks wisdom from the dead.
The cathars realized they had not tracked her—she had led them here.
"Never thought I'd see the day I'd be wishing to see just a plain old werewolf." —Raf Gyel of the Quiver of Kessig
". . . heck, I'd settle for anything that even resembled a werewolf." —Raf Gyel of the Quiver of Kessig
"I'm afraid it's bad news."
"My village's fear drove me into the wild . . ."
". . . and I will bring the fury of the wild back to my village."
"A werewolf's howl is terrifying, to be sure. But this . . . this was a chilling sound I somehow felt. I fear what will reply to it." —Alena, trapper of Kessig
The sweet taste of hope's promise.
The bitter taste of life's only certainty.
A golden helix streaked skyward from the Helvault. A thunderous explosion shattered the silver monolith and Avacyn emerged, free from her prison at last.
If it comes for you, die boldly or die swiftly—for die you will.
Its footsteps of today are the lakes of tomorrow.
